articles.title: "I'd kick his a—s" - Charles Barkley brutally assessed Barack Obama's chances in a 1-on-1
articles.summary: Barkley issued a bold response when asked about playing 1-on-1 with ex-President Obama.
articles.body:
Charles Barkley can get away with almost anything, even when it arguably involves the most powerful man on the planet. Known for his candid and outspoken nature, the 1993 Phoenix Suns MVP refuses to change no matter what, which is also what makes him so beloved and endearing. Chuck is no doubt one of the funniest people to watch on television.

Beyond the jokes and messing around, Barkley also has a serious side, especially when it comes to politics and social issues. There's a lot more to the Chuckster than basketball, which is also why he has close connections with people from other walks of life. This also includes the 44th President of the United States of America, Barack Obama .

President Obama has been an avid basketball fan since childhood. He played on the varsity team at Hawaii Punahou School and was part of the 1979 state championship team. Although his political career took precedence over the years, the former POTUS always found a way to stay connected to the hardwood.

So it's no surprise that Barack shares close ties with some of the NBA's biggest names, including Charles, who once shared some interesting insights into President Obama's basketball skills.

"He's a lefty. He always goes left. And if you just stand there, I'm not sure if you were to open up the right side, he could go right at all," said Chuck while addressing the 44th POTUS during a 2010 appearance on TBS Conan.

As for a 1-on-1 matchup, Barkley made it clear the former U.S. president had no chance against him.

"Oh yeah, I mean, I'm an old fat guy now, but I'd kick his a—s," said Barkley, who has developed a close rapport with the former President over time.

The two stalwarts of sports and politics first met in 2005 when Barkley was promoting his book, "Who's Afraid of a Large Black Man?" During this time, he had the opportunity to interview Obama, then the newly elected Senator from Illinois.

The interview focused on sensitive issues like racism in the United States. The interaction left Barkley highly impressed, who eventually became one of Obama's most vocal supporters. A prime example of this was Chuck shooting an endorsement video for the former President as he ran for president in 2008.

The two met again for a sit-down in 2014 ahead of the 63rd All-Star Game. However, this time the discussion centered more on basketball, whether it was the GOAT debate between Michael Jordan and LeBron James, or the President getting time for pickup ball. They also shed some light on the country's political situation.

As time passed, Barkley and Obama remained in touch, collaborating on various social and community initiatives. These include "My Brother's Keeper Alliance," an initiative aimed at improving the lives of young men of color. They have also been instrumental in supporting HBCUs through donations, grants, and scholarships.

The 2021 NBC Special "Roll Up Your Sleeves" was yet another example, featuring the former POTUS teaming up with Barkley and Shaquille O'Neal to educate communities about the importance of COVID-19 vaccination. Chuck has also made financial contributions to the Obama Foundation on multiple occasions.

Given their philanthropic nature, it would be a sight to behold if Barkley and Obama could host a 1-on-1 with the proceeds going to charity.

articles.title: LeBron James plays point forward as 76ers offense shines in first look at new star-studded lineup
articles.summary: Philadelphia's offense looked like a well-oiled machine in its first look with LeBron James in the lineup.
articles.body:
The arrival of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown to a 76ers lineup that already features Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe raised a significant question in Philadelphia: Who's going to be on the ball?

James made his 76ers preseason debut Thursday against the Brooklyn Nets alongside each of his aforementioned teammates. He provided an early look at an answer.

The ball ran through James on Thursday and to strong effect. James played primarily in his point forward role, and Philadelphia's offense was well-oiled from the opening tip of an eventual 114-108 loss.

James assisted on two of Philadelphia's first three field goals, including a nice no-look dish through the lane to find Edgecombe on the baseline under the bucket.

Philadelphia's second field goal started with a hockey assist from James.

James found Joel Embiid with a bounce pass of the pick-and-roll on the wing, and Embiid drove to dish it under the hope to Brown for an easy dunk.

Philadelphia's ball movement was crisp, and the 76ers didn't look like a unit playing together for the first time while shooting 7 of 8 from the field to start the game.

James was content to facilitate and didn't take his first field goal attempt until 4:54 remained on the first-quarter clock. That was a drive to the bucket that resulted in a foul and two free throws.

He finished the first quarter with four points and five assists with all of his points arriving at the free thrown line. The 76ers held a 33-32 lead as Maxey carried the scoring load with 10 points.

James didn't log his first official field-goal attempt in the box score until a reverse layup on a nice pass from Maxey over the top of Brooklyn's defense. James converted for his fifth and sixth points with 6:52 remaining in the second quarter.

By halftime, the 76ers held a 58-56 lead. James finished with 10 points, 5 assists, 4 rebounds, 2 turnovers and 1 steal in 18 minutes. Eight of his points came at the line as he shot 1 for 1 from the field, and he sat for the second half.

Maxey led the 76ers in the first half with 14 points on 5 of 8 shooting from the field. Embiid had 6 points, 3 rebounds and 7 turnovers at the break, and Brown had 8 points on 2-of-4 shooting from the floor.

As a team, the 76ers shot 16 of 28 (57%) in the first half with assists on 12 of their 16 made field goals. Ball control was the biggest challenge as they committed 14 turnovers before the second half in which they deferred largely to the bench.

Brown led all 76ers for the game with 18 points as he played well into the third quarter.

This, of course, was a preseason exhibition and by no means a blueprint for Philadelphia's offense this season. But it would certainly be no surprise if this is how the 76ers intend to frequently operate once the games actually matter.

articles.title: LeBron James Makes 76ers Preseason Debut, Final Box Score Stats & Highlights for Embiid, Brown, More
articles.summary: A new era for the Philadelphia 76ers began on Thursday.
articles.body:
A new era for the Philadelphia 76ers began on Thursday.

LeBron James made his preseason debut for the Sixers on Thursday ahead of his 24th NBA season. James took the court alongside his new teammates, Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey, against the Brooklyn Nets.

James started for the 76ers and played most of the first half, but didn't play in the second half, as did Philadelphia's other stars. Considering it's the preseason, it's likely James, Embiid, Brown and Maxey won't get too much action as they gear up for the regular season.

While James didn't play too much, he seemed to find an early connection with some of his teammates.

Brown played in Philadelphia's preseason opener against New York, but Thursday marked the first time all four stars were on the court together.

Having added James and Brown this summer, the 76ers have high expectations and all the talent to compete for a title. Key for this year's squad will be health, though, as James is 41 years old and Embiid has a lengthy injury history.

The Sixers will have to manage their stars' playing time strategically to ensure they're ready to go for the playoffs, while also allowing them to find their identity throughout the season.

Thursday's game was a preview of what's to come in what should be an exciting era for the 76ers, who will look to bring home their first title since 1983.

articles.title: Is Kyrie Irving playing today’s game? Latest status on Dallas Mavericks guard before preseason game against Rockets
articles.summary: Kyrie Irving will play in one of the two preseason games Dallas has against the Houston Rockets at The Venetian Arena in Macao, but the Mavericks have not
articles.body: Kyrie Irving will play in one of the two preseason games Dallas has against the Houston Rockets at The Venetian Arena in Macao, but the Mavericks have not said which one. Coach Dusty May confirmed the split on Thursday and left the choice open. Friday’s game is the first chance, and Sunday’s is the other. Irving has not played in a game since March 3, 2025, when he tore his left ACL. Dallas went 26-56 in 2025-26 without him. A full availability report is due before Friday’s tipoff, so the answer should come soon.Is Kyrie Irving playing tonight against the Rockets?Yes, in one game but not both. The opener is Friday at 7 a.m. CST, and Sunday’s rematch tips at 5 a.m. CST. Irving was cleared for the trip with no restrictions, so the split is about workload, not health. Christian Clark of The Athletic reported May also plans to use a limited roster in both games. He's now in Macao.The nine-time All-Star is 34 and coming off a long layoff. A grade 2 calf strain in December cost him about eight weeks and pushed the timeline back further. Two games in three days is a lot for a first outing in 19 months, which is why one appearance makes sense. For viewers in Dallas, Friday is the friendlier hour. Whichever game he plays, fans will get a first live look at Irving next to teenager Cooper Flagg.Dereck Lively II is still recovering from December surgery on his right foot, and Santi Aldama has been limited since camp opened after a March procedure and injection on his right knee. No. 9 pick Morez Johnson Jr. dealt with lower leg soreness but is expected to play Friday, according to Brad Townsend of The Dallas Morning News. He played only two Summer League games, averaging 18.5 points, 6.5 rebounds, 2.5 steals and 3.0 blocks. Daniel Gafford and Moussa Cisse are the two big men who have stayed healthy. Further updates from the team will determine Irving’s availability.What has Irving said about the ACL tear and coming home?He also looked back on the ACL tear in an unusual way. Irving has called it the best thing that happened to him, saying the break let him spend more time with his family and address parts of his body he had overlooked. He does not want to miss that much time again, he added, and he credited a support system through some rocky stretches.Thursday gave him a chance to thank fans for 19 months of patience. “I want to hear them yell,” he said. Dallas acquired him in a February 2023 trade, and he won the 2016 title with Cleveland. The team returns home after Sunday’s game, and he sees the preseason games on Oct. 14 and Oct. 16 as a way to ease back in front of the crowd. articles.title: “I do think the Clippers are cursed”: Ex-Warriors champion makes bold revelation involving Steve Ballmer following a series of unfortunate events for the team
articles.summary: Last year, the Dallas Mavericks saw the wrath of fans and critics following Luka Doncic’s trade.
articles.body: Last year, the Dallas Mavericks saw the wrath of fans and critics following Luka Doncic’s trade. After a series of unfortunate events, the team is rebuilding its status and roster. This year, the Clippers are in the same position, even worse. They have been under vehement criticism from the league, of course, and have had to endure huge punishments. Now, Ex-Warriors champion Matt Barnes shared that he had a solution before all this, as he suggested a name change for the team in a proposal to Steve Ballmer.Barnes thinks the Los Angeles Clippers need a new name. In his interview with TMZ Sports, the former Warriors champion called the franchise cursed and linked the idea to the salary cap scandal involving Kawhi Leonard. Barnes says he gave owner Steve Ballmer the same advice in 2014, when Ballmer bought the team, and people laughed. Since then the NBA has stripped five first-round picks, fined Ballmer and banned him for a year. Leonard is gone too. The Clippers are now working to win back fans who feel let down.Why does Matt Barnes think the Clippers are cursed?Matt Barnes made the pitch in 2014, when Steve Ballmer bought the team for $2 billion. Nobody took it seriously. “I do think the Clippers are cursed,” Barnes told TMZ Sports, adding the franchise needs a new name because the bad energy never left.The latest trouble brought the old joke back. The NBA ruled that the Clippers circumvented the salary cap in deals involving Kawhi Leonard, a case first exposed by a Pulitzer Prize-winning investigation from the Pablo Torre Finds Out podcast. The league’s 35-page report said the team helped arrange third-party deals between Leonard and vendors, then got those companies to sign by offering them business from the club.The penalties were heavy. Besides the loss of five first-round picks, Ballmer received a $30 million fine and a one-year ban from all league and team activities. Leonard was fined $700,000, and other team employees were also penalized too.The team has dealt with scandal before. Donald Sterling’s ban in 2014 pushed the sale to Ballmer forward, and the franchise has spent the years since trying to move past that image. A cap scandal twelve years later has pulled it back into the same spotlight. A new name would not undo either episode, though it would give the Clippers a visible fresh start.How have the Clippers responded since the NBA ruling?The first reaction was anger. The Clippers strongly rejected the findings and sent commissioner Adam Silver a letter calling the probe a “witch hunt.” The letter claimed Ballmer spent nearly $50 million to fund the probe, which an independent law firm ran. Ballmer has long denied the allegations.A legal fight never looked promising. The NBA said the discipline was agreed with the players’ union and is final and binding, and league bylaws offer no route to contest the investigation. Ballmer chose to accept the punishment and skip a legal battle.The tone changed at the team’s media day. Interim president of basketball operations Trent Redden told fans they deserved to hear from the team sooner, “and for that we’re sorry.” Redden said the club has been hearing the concerns of its fan base and wants to rebuild trust and keep its promises. articles.summary: "De niña, sueñas a lo grande. Por eso lloré más con este trofeo, porque la A'ja de 15 años no estaba aquí sentada soñando con ser cinco veces MVP"
articles.body: A'ja Wilson, jugadora de Las Vegas Aces, ganó su quinto MVP de la WNBA, lo que la convirtió además en la primera jugadora de la historia en obtener este galardón en tres temporadas consecutivas. "De niña, sueñas a lo grande, escribes tus metas y nunca te imaginas que podrás cumplirlas. Por eso lloré más con este trofeo, porque la A'ja de 15 años no estaba aquí sentada soñando con ser cinco veces MVP. No soñaba con ser tres veces campeona", dijo la pívot de las Aces poco después de conocer la noticia. "Soñaba con sobrevivir en este mundo. Así que para mí, estar aquí sentada rodeada de estos trofeos... significa mucho más", agregó. Wilson recibió 65 de los 74 votos para el primer lugar y nueve para el segundo. Superó en la votación a la novata de las Minnesota Lynx, Olivia Miles. Wilson promedió 26,2 puntos, 9,4 rebotes y 3,2 asistencias por partido en la temporada regular y lideró a las Aces hasta el tercer mejor balance de la liga. La jugadora será homenajeada el viernes antes del tercer partido de las semifinales de los 'playoffs', en el que su equipo se juega quedar eliminado. Las Aces pierden 0-2 en la serie que las enfrenta a las Golden State Valkyries, el equipo con el segundo mejor balance en la temporada regular.

articles.title: Everything LeBron James Said After 76ers Preseason Debut on New Teammates, Being Away from Family
articles.summary: LeBron James began his next chapter on Thursday.
articles.body:
LeBron James began his next chapter on Thursday.

The veteran made his preseason debut with the Philadelphia 76ers against the Brooklyn Nets, posting 10 points, five assists and four rebounds in a 114-108 loss.

James is no stranger to everything that comes with preparing for the season, but this year is a new challenge as he gets adjusted to a new team and a new city. At the end of the day, however, it felt natural when he stepped on the hardwood.

"It felt a little different, obviously, wearing the uniform," James told reporters. "But the game is the game, and the game is being played on the floor. And I was happy to log some minutes with the guys that we've been going at each other in practice for the last two weeks... It was great to finally just go out there and log some time and log some minutes."

James had an eventful offseason with plenty of travel followed by his intense free agency process. He's now tasked with getting back into the groove of things ahead of an 82-game season while balancing being with a new organization.

"Obviously, I have my routine, but when you go through an offseason, you've got to remember what your routine was again, no matter how many, how long you've been in it," James told reporters . "So, just thinking about, like, which buses do I remember taking, you know? What was my routine when I got over to the arena? How do I get ready for the game and things of that nature.

"So all that stuff plays a part. So I'm still getting into the whole everything, on the court and off the court, living and also being around these guys every day. It's a lot of adjustment for me, but, every day we'll get better and better."

Living in New York and playing in Philadelphia means James is away from his family often, but he said having great teammates has made the transition much easier.

"Every day it's getting better. Obviously, I'm gonna have some days where days will be better than others," he said. "But when I get to the facility and I'm around these guys, it definitely helps. We've got good energy, good spirit. Obviously the basketball game, what it brings to all of us is a sense of togetherness and fun. It's fun to go to work."

James played limited minutes in his preseason debut, which wasn't much of a surprise. The 41-year-old has a long season ahead of him and will look to stay healthy and help his fellow stars Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey deliver a championship to Philadelphia.

articles.title: LeBron James: NBA superstar makes Philadelphia 76ers debut in pre-season defeat by Brooklyn Nets
articles.summary: LeBron James says it's "going to take some time" for his new team-mates to gel after suffering defeat on his debut for the Philadelphia 76ers in a pre-season game.
articles.body:
LeBron James said it's "going to take some time" for his new team-mates to gel after suffering defeat on his debut for the Philadelphia 76ers in a pre-season game.

The 41-year-old American joined the 76ers in July for what he says will be his final contract in the NBA following a glittering career.

James is the highest points scorer in the history of the league and is entering a record-extending 24th NBA season.

James scored 10 points and added four rebounds, five assists and a steal in 18 first-half minutes as his side fell to a 114-108 defeat by the Brooklyn Nets.

"We're still trying to put each other in the position to be successful and complement each other the best way we can on the floor. But it's going to take some time," said James.

"Tonight was a good sample size for us to build on."

James played alongside new team-mates Joel Embiid, VJ Edgecombe, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown, with the latter leading the scoring with 18 points.

James has won titles with every NBA side he has played for, including two with the Miami Heat, one with the Cleveland Cavaliers and another with the Los Angeles Lakers.

He left the Lakers this summer after spending eight years with the franchise.

James has been named the NBA's Most Valuable Player four times, all between 2009 and 2013, and has been an NBA All-Star the last 22 seasons running.

articles.title: A'ja Wilson becomes first five-time MVP in WNBA history with third-straight award
articles.summary: A ceremony marking her record-extending fifth MVP award will take place on Friday night, but A'ja Wilson will not take part before a must-win game.
articles.body:
While a ceremony marking her latest historic achievement will take place on Friday night, A'ja Wilson wants no part of it.

The 30-year-old Las Vegas Aces star stands peerless after becoming the first five-time Most Valuable Player (MVP) in WNBA history, and was informed of her unprecedented third-straight award by a former US vice-president.

But recent history means Wilson has no interest in joining the celebrations which will be held on her behalf.

When the Aces held a pre-game ceremony to honour Wilson last year, as is tradition for the MVP winner, they went on to lose game one of their play-off semi-final.

They also lost heavily following similar celebrations after receiving their championship rings in May.

Before a must-win third game in their best-of-five semi-final against the Golden State Valkyries, Wilson is taking no chances.

"I love the fans, but I will not be doing that," she said. "I will be warming up with my team. Everyone knows how much of a competitor I am [and] what my main focus is."

No other WNBA player has won more than three MVP awards.

Having also won in 2020 and 2022, Wilson joins NBA legends Michael Jordan and Bill Russell as five-time MVP winners. Kareem Abdul-Jabbar won six.

"I've said [before] 'Take her off Mount Rushmore, she's Everest," Aces coach Becky Hammon said.

"Now, I'm taking her off Everest and I just have to put her on a different planet."

Wilson, who received 65 of 74 first-place votes, received a voice message from former vice-president Kamala Harris delivering the news.

Despite her extensive list of honours, Wilson was very emotional after receiving her latest MVP award on the Aces' practice court.

"When you dream as a young girl, you dream so big and you write your goals out and you just never imagine you will be able to check them off," Wilson said

"I think that's why I cried a little bit harder on this one because 15-year-old A'ja wasn't sitting up here dreaming about being a five-time MVP, she wasn't dreaming about being a three-time champion, she was dreaming about surviving this world."

Wilson averaged 26.2 points to lead the league in scoring for the third straight season.

An eight-time All-Star, she registered at least 20 points in 33 games - the third-highest single-season streak in WNBA history, and tied her own WNBA single-season record of scoring at least 30 points in 13 games.

Wilson has won three league titles with the Aces - achieved in the past four years - but they face elimination in this year's semi-finals as they trail Golden State 2-0.

articles.title: LeBron James stars in NBA preseason debut but Nets defeat 76ers
articles.summary: All-time leading scorer LeBron James makes 76ers debut following LA Lakers switch in NBA preseason, but Nets claim win.
articles.body:
NBA superstar LeBron James delivered a solid first half in his first preseason game for Philadelphia, but the new-look 76ers fell 114-108 to the Nets in Brooklyn.

James, the NBA’s all-time leading scorer, announced in July that he had signed a two-year, $8m deal with the 76ers, ending weeks of speculation over where the four-time NBA champion would land as a free agent after eight seasons and one title with the Los Angeles Lakers.

The 41-year-old superstar, entering a record-extending 24th NBA season, won two titles with Miami, another with Cleveland and a fourth with the Lakers, and is aiming to help the Sixers win their first title since Julius Erving led the club to the crown 43 years ago.

Thursday’s game marked his first chance to line up alongside new teammates Joel Embiid, VJ Edgecombe, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown – a new arrival from the Boston Celtics.

“It felt a little different,” James said. “Obviously, just wearing a new uniform, but the game is the game.

“We’re still trying to put each other in a position to be successful and complement each other the best way we can out on the floor,” he added. “But it’s going to take some time. Tonight was a good sample size for us to build on.”

James scored 10 points, connecting on his lone shot from the floor and making all eight of his free-throw attempts. He added four rebounds, five assists and a steal in 18:04 minutes in the first half.

Brown led all scorers with 18 points. Julius Randle had 14 for the Nets, who outscored the Sixers 37-23 in the third quarter to take control.

LeBron James captures NBA spotlight again

But all eyes were on James, starting with his first signature pre-game chalk-toss in a 76ers uniform.

James smoothly directed the Sixers’ offence in his time on the floor, making all five of his assists in the first quarter and combining effectively with Maxey.

“I think there was some really good things happening, you know, right off the bat,” 76ers coach Nick Nurse said after seeing his starters together for the first time.

“A bunch of back cuts and good passing, etc, there were segments where obviously we turned the ball over a lot … just the little clunky segments, too. But, again, it’s preseason, first time they’re together.

“I think you look at it as what’s good and what are the learning experiences, things that we can improve.”

The 76ers have two more preseason games, both against Boston, before opening the NBA regular season against the defending champion New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on October 20.

James’s arrival has already found the 76ers battling outside “noise”.

James took to Instagram to refute a report from a play-by-play announcer during the team’s first preseason game on Monday that James had admonished Embiid for being late to a practice.

“He ain’t been late, so stop the lie,” James posted.

James had acknowledged at the team’s media day last month that such outside hubbub around the 76ers would be “doubled, tripled and quadrupled now that I’m here”.

articles.title: Jemele Hill demands harsh punishment for WNBA ref who lied to Breanna Stewart in Game 2 loss
articles.summary: Sports writer Jemele Hill has called out the official who was at the centre of controversy after the New York Liberty’s 101-98 loss to the Atlanta Dream in G...
articles.body:
Sports writer Jemele Hill has called out the official who was at the centre of controversy after the New York Liberty's 101-98 loss to the Atlanta Dream in Game 2 of the WNBA second round.

As the Dream were shooting free throws, Breanna Stewart was lining up to box out and collect the rebound for a final attempt. She asked the official, Kevin Fahy, if the Liberty had a reset timeout, which would help them advance the ball higher up the court and get an easier look for a three-pointer, but Stewart said she was denied at that time.

However, the Liberty did have a reset timeout and after the game, the eight-time All-Star revealed what had happened between the free throws in her post-game press conference.

"This is not blaming the refs, but when I ask both refs if we have a reset timeout at the end and they tell us no, and then we leave the game with a reset timeout, it's pretty frustrating," Stewart said.

After the game, clips have been making the rounds of the interaction between Stewart and the official, which has convinced Hill of what had happened.

Lead official Fatou Cissoko-Stephens said that the Liberty were informed about the reset timeout, which is different from what Stewart revealed in her press conference.

However, Hill had her decision after watching the clips and she posted her thoughts on X.

"So the official straight up lied. That official should be taken off the rest of the playoffs," tweeted Hill.

With 4.3 seconds still left, Liberty started the play on their baseline and they did have a final attempt, but the heave from Stewart was short and led to their loss on the night.

Now the team will have to focus on Game 3, which will be the decider. Losing that will end their playoff run and Stewart's pursuit of her fourth WNBA championship.

The 2019-20 NBA season was a unique campaign due to the intervention of the COVID-19 pandemic. Following a brief hiatus, the season resumed in the Orlando Bubble.

Kanter, at the time, was a member of the Boston Celtics, and recently revealed a 'disgusting' truth about his teammates.

Enes Kanter says Boston Celtics players had unlimited OnlyFans access during NBA Bubble

Kanter shared how Celtics players had unlimited access to OnlyFans during the NBA Bubble and how he stayed away from this practice.

"This happened with the Celtics. I mean, which was disgusting, I'm glad that I did not do it. So this is not the NBA. I don't know who did that. They were passing away this some kind of like a password.

"So you can literally just go on and watch any OnlyFans model you want for free," Kanter told Clay Travis.

He added, "So, they put this like code on a paper. They were just passing. I'm like, 'What is this?' So they explained to me. I'm like, 'I'm good. I don't want it.

"… I don't want to watch someone's daughter, someone's whatever just getting naked.' And I just wouldn't do it, I have better morals."

articles.title: 1 Player Every NBA Team Should Trade This Season
articles.summary: NBA rosters must be finalized ahead of the fast-approaching opening night.
articles.body:
NBA rosters must be finalized ahead of the fast-approaching opening night.

It's a much more temporary process than it sounds.

Because rosters are never really locked into place. They might be secured for certain stretches, but there is almost always a chance to change them. Just like there are always countless front-office executives figuring out what, if any, changes are needed.

That's why we can sit this far out from that opening tip getting tossed and already identify the one player each franchise should trade away during the upcoming campaign. Some are stars, some are roster-fillers; some are obvious, some are far less so. But all of them have reasons to be routed somewhere between now and February's trade deadline.

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GSW | HOU | IND | LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN | NOP | NYK | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX | POR | SAC | SAS | TOR | UTA | WAS

The Hawks, who landed Landale at last season's deadline, extended the backup big man's stay in Atlanta with a one-year, $14.1 million pact this summer. That's a healthy investment in a 30-year-old reserve, even while acknowledging the value he brings with his spacing, rebounding and physicality.

Maybe the Hawks are just huge fans, or perhaps they wanted another mid-sized salary on the books in case they needed to match money in a significant trade.

If Atlanta feels the need for a consolidation trade, Landale should be part of the outgoing package. He'd have plug-and-play appeal for trade partners, and the Hawks might welcome the chance to throw more minutes at young bigs Asa Newell and Zuby Ejiofor.

It would be ideal to provide this answer closer to the first-quarter mark of the campaign, since no one knows how this Jaylen Brown-less version of Boston will look.

If contending still seems possible, then maybe that would embolden the Celtics to broker a huge blockbuster built around Paul George's colossal salary and draft assets. If this group is obviously more than one player away, moving Derrick White for trade chips to cash in at a later date could be the right call.

For now, though, this feels like a safe middle ground. Hauser has a relatively modest salary ( $10.8 million ), a coveted role (6'7" sharpshooter) and plenty of playoff experience. He would not be difficult to shop. He also might be somewhat simple to replace internally with some combination of Baylor Scheierman, Jordan Walsh and Hugo González.

The Nets are another team that could benefit from the passage of time to identify a trade candidate. If they don't seem any more competitive than they have of late (three consecutive 50-plus-loss seasons), then high-scoring veterans Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle would feature prominently among the league's most logical trade candidates.

But that feels too pessimistic for this point on the hoops calendar, doesn't it? Optimism peaks every October, so let's at least allow for the possibility that these Nets might be punchier. Maybe even a Play-In participant if everything breaks right.

Regardless how things play out, Mann seems eminently expendable. The $31.5 million he'll make over this season and next doesn't align with his on-court contributions, which last season included just 7.2 points in 24.3 minutes a night. He wouldn't have trade value on his own, but his contract could be a helpful math tool in a larger transaction.

The Hornets could be in wait-and-see mode for a while after stunningly splitting from LaMelo Ball this summer. Their timeline almost surely shifted this offseason, although the further developments of Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel will decide by how much.

That probably takes major trades off the table for now, but if anything does arise, look for Williams and his expiring $14.3 million salary to be involved.

That's not necessarily an egregious amount for someone with his toughness, defensive versatility, outside shooting (career 37.8 percent) and postseason experience. It's just probably more than Charlotte would prefer to play a backup, especially if it wants to see more of 2024's No. 6 pick Tidjane Salaün.

Bulls fans might be screaming for Patrick Williams here, but the lack of market interest torpedoes that take. A clean-slate split might be best for both parties, but Chicago would have to heavily incentivize someone to take back Williams and the $56 million he's owed through 2028-29.

Powell, on the other hand, could be a great get for the right win-now team . The 33-year-old has experience, a powerful scoring punch (21.8 points over the past two seasons), a reliable three-ball (career 39.6 percent) and a digestible deal ( $21.5 million this season, $22.6 million team option for next).

He would make sense in a lot of different places, just not in Chicago where the timeline split between Powell and his young teammates appears cavernous.

Truth be told, there isn't an obvious trade worth making for the Cavaliers right now. Between Peyton Watson's arrival, Jaylon Tyson's development and the addition of #MuscleWatch grand champion Mario Hezonja, hopes have never been higher for Cleveland's forward spots.

If this doesn't work, though, Cleveland's next attempt to solve the puzzle almost certainly would include the sacrifice of a core four member. And if the Cavs ever go that route, Allen would likely land on the chopping block.

The spacing constraints of his pairing with Evan Mobley haven't gone away, and Allen's rim-running role seems the easiest to replace (perhaps by Mobley himself). It's also a coveted archetype, and he's on a good contract (three years, $90.7 million), so it wouldn't be difficult to drum up interest.

The Mavericks have a 19-year-old centerpiece in Cooper Flagg. So, forgive the basketball world for doubting Dallas' insistence that it still has a need for Irving, a 34-year-old who just lost a full season to an ACL recovery.

"The question that's being asked around the league is, for how long? How long is this fit with Kyrie and the Mavericks?" ESPN's Tim MacMahon said. "... Could there come a time when it makes sense for both sides to find a contender for Kyrie to go to? These are the kinds of things that people around the league will be monitoring leading up to the trade deadline."

Suitors are surfacing already , and this season hasn't even tipped yet. Irving could be a great on-court fit with Flagg, and it would still make sense for Dallas, which doesn't control its first-round pick until 2031 , to explore deals that swap out Irving for younger players, draft assets or a combination of the two.

It's too early to say the Nuggets need to explore the type of wholesale changes that would sacrifice the likes of Jamal Murray or Aaron Gordon. And, frankly, if Denver were going to deal either Christian Braun or Cameron Johnson, it probably would've done so this summer instead of letting Peyton Watson walk.

So, the spotlight instead lands on Holmes, who appears buried on the frontcourt depth chart but could pique the interest of the right long-term shopper.

He has virtually no track record at this level—he lost his would-be rookie season to a torn Achilles, then spent much of his sophomore campaign in the G League—but teams could view him as a flier worth taking. He's only 24 years old and was a first-round pick in 2024 (No. 22), and he still boasts an intriguing blend of length, bounce and long-range shooting.

The Pistons ponied up big bucks to ensure both Ausar Thompson and Jalen Duren remain alongside Cade Cunningham. What they didn't do, though, is find the scoring and creation support he remains without.

If it's obviously an issue again—he was essentially tasked with one-man-army duties during their last playoff run—they'll have to go hunt for that player on the trade market. And they'd almost certainly need Robinson and his $16 million salary (nothing guaranteed for next season) to facilitate the swap.

It would be risky for a club so squeezed for spacing as it is to ditch a decorated shooter from distance, but the combination of Isaiah Joe and Kevin Huerter can help cover the void. And if 2025 second-round pick Chaz Lanier looks rotation-ready, things would get even easier on that front.

Golden State Warriors: Kristaps Porziņģis

This could be wrong, but it doesn't seem like an Earth-shattering acquisition is in the cards for this club. If the Dubs brokered the kind of blockbuster that would require using the salaries tied to Jimmy Butler or Draymond Green, they probably would've made that change this summer, not midseason.

They should still be probing for upgrades, though. They need to give Stephen Curry more help, and with Porziņģis once again stuck in a worrisome health situation , he seems incapable of providing it.

But his $20 million salary (and tiny $3 million guarantee for next season) could be a gear-greaser for that kind of get. He can't have much (if any) standalone value given the constant availability concerns, but teams with big plans for the loaded 2027 free agency class could want to get their hands on that contract.

If these Rockets fail to lift-off, there could be much bigger names at play. They could dangle Alperen Şengün in hopes of going huge-game hunting. If point guard remains a problem, one or both of Fred VanVleet and Reed Sheppard might get sent packing. If chemistry issues remain, they might decide Kevin Durant just isn't the right fit.

We just don't know if any of that will happen, though. In fact, there are legitimate hopes that none of it will, since this team—a 52-game winner each of the past two seasons—has reasons to believe that VanVleet's return might get everything aligned yet.

If those beliefs manifest into any kind of step forward, the Rockets may merely work the margins during trade season. And it would be hard to see how Capela, a $7 million third-string center, wouldn't be involved in that activity.

The Pacers placed their trade wager last season, ultimately parting with young players and multiple first-round picks (including this year's fifth overall) to plug veteran big man Ivica Zubac into their Myles Turner-sized hole on the interior.

Indiana probably can't stomach another sizable shakeup for the foreseeable future. It may not need one anyway, if the return of Tyrese Haliburton—engineer of this team's run to the 2025 NBA Finals—gets this group back into the contending conversation.

Shifting things to the smaller-scale side, then, maybe Sheppard gets moved to fill a niche need elsewhere. The 25-year-old has hinted at three-and-D ability, but he might need more minutes than Indiana can afford to give him to fully realize that potential.

The Clippers could be fully open for business if they're really worried about getting the cupboards restocked after paying such a pick-heavy price from the cap circumvention investigation. But with a slew of veterans on the roster, and optimism around Brandon Ingram's recovery, maybe L.A. wants to give this core a chance before stripping everything down to the foundation.

Even if that's the case, though, Lopez seems like he's losing his utility to this team. He may have already been surpassed by Isaiah Jackson on the depth chart, and the Clippers will want to keep the runway clear whenever Yanic Konan Niederhäuser is ready to return from March foot surgery.

Lopez, who will turn 39 by season's end, would only appeal to win-right-this-second clubs, but the ones who fit that description and need a backup big might be very interested. His numbers might be trending down, but he still provides a helpful blend of offensive spacing and defensive paint protection.

Surprised not to see Dalton Knecht in this spot? Well, it's much less a vote of confidence for him and much more about skepticism that he'll even make the opening-night roster.

And if Knecht gets cut, that means his fellow chopping-block resident , Vanderbilt, holds solo status as the most logical trade candidate on the roster.

The Lakers have clearly concluded that Vanderbilt's defensive impact can't offset his offensive limitations, but other teams could compute things differently. The right suitor might see him as capable of getting back to being a defense-first energizer.

Hopefully, after 12 NBA seasons, Grant understands how to impart his hoops wisdom and veteran know-how in a hurry. Because despite just arriving in Memphis this summer as part of the Ja Morant trade, Grant's stay could be of the abbreviated variety.

"Sources say Jerami Grant is excited to embrace his role as the veteran leader of this team entering the 2026-27 season," Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints wrote. "Looking ahead, he will be a prime trade candidate as the season progresses."

Grant, a near-19-point scorer last season, still has something to give a win-now team, but Memphis isn't one of those. The Grizzlies could grow into that label over time, but doing so would require—among a number of other things—giving as many reps as possible to young forwards Jaylen Wells, Cameron Boozer, GG Jackson, Karim López and Taylor Hendricks.

The Heat, admittedly, probably aren't looking to move Jović. They'd be selling low, for starters, after a disappointing 2025-26 season. They'd also be giving up all the things he could potentially give this team, like shotmaking, ball-handling and secondary playmaking.

Then again, they need tangible talents and not theoretical contributions, so if Jović encounters another rough patch, maybe Miami concludes he's just not ready to support this now Giannis Antetokounmpo-led group. That's assuming Jović even gets enough floor time to sink or swim, which is hardly a given when the 4 and 5 spots (where he has almost exclusively played) feature Antetokounmpo, Bam Adebayo, Bobby Portis, Nick Richards, Simone Fontecchio and (in spot minutes) Andrew Wiggins.

The Heat also need trade chips, since they emptied their collection to get Giannis. Jović, who turned 23 in June, should still qualify as such given his age and flashes of unique offensive ability for a 6'10" forward.

While the Bucks finally split from Giannis Antetokounmpo this summer, their roster-resetting work is far from finished. Milwaukee needs to continue stockpiling assets in hopes of finding its next franchise face, and both Turner and Kel'el Ware could be a part of that effort.

"Already front-office executives around the league are chirping about how the Bucks are a team that could be targeted because they still have something a lot of teams wish they had: Big men who can shoot 3s and protect the rim," Yahoo Sports' Kevin O'Connor wrote.

Ware might be far from a proven commodity, but it's still tough to see the Bucks facing a real dilemma when considering which floor-spacing big man to keep. Turner is 30; Ware is 22. Ten out of 10 rebuilders would opt to keep the latter.

Like some other aggressive buyers, the Wolves have largely cleared out their trade candidates already. The young talent that remains on the roster feels largely like it's there because the front office wants it to be.

But Williams could be different. He only joined the group in August and arrived by way of a cost-cutting move intended to clear space before signing Jonathan Kuminga. For the Wolves, Williams might simply be the means to an end.

He could, however, hold some reclamation-project appeal to the right team—one not hoping to contend this season. Williams has been utterly unproductive through two NBA seasons (career 7.3 player efficiency rating ), but he is 21 years old and a recent top-10 pick (No. 10 in 2024), so maybe hope isn't lost just yet.

New Orleans has nearly an entire roster full of trade candidates. None, though, carries the same urgency to trade as Poole.

His $34 million salary expires at season's end, so the Pels are up against a use-it-or-lose-it ticking clock. Some clubs could appreciate the flexibility that would eventually come with his acquisition. Others might be willing to pay that short-term price for a spark-plug rental, especially if Poole shows off his shooting range, scoring touch and slippery handles.

The Pelicans could also see value in giving Poole's minutes (23.9 last season) to someone else. At point guard, they need to either showcase Dejounte Murray as a trade candidate or follow his lead to Play-In participation, plus develop 2025 lottery pick Jeremiah Fears. On the perimeter, Poole could get pressed for playing time by Trey Murphy III, Herbert Jones, Saddiq Bey and newcomer Bennedict Mathurin.

There are, to be clear, far juicier names being tossed around in New York. But the Knicks wouldn't just dismantle a championship core for financial reasons, would they? Fingers crossed.

Trading Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart or even Miles McBride feels too dramatic for a team that finally had its banner-raising breakthrough after such an agonizingly long wait.

The conversation is entirely different with Dadiet, who has shown so little since arriving as the No. 25 pick in 2024 that he may already have negative trade value . But if New York needs $3 million in expiring salary to get a trade across the finish line, he'd be a no-brainer inclusion.

The Thunder had to make a few financial cuts to their rotation this summer, but just ask Sorber about how absurdly deep this roster remains.

Because unless the interior-bound 6'9", 250-pounder can handle power-forward duties, it could be a while before Sorber ever sees the floor. Center seems totally off-limits with Isaiah Hartenstein starting, and OKC having both Jaylin Williams (a key contributor throughout his four-plus-year tenure with the team) and Mr. Automatic Aday Mara on the bench.

Sorber, who is still working his way back from the ACL tear that erased his would-be rookie season, has no immediate or obvious paths to playing time. With the interior this crowded, he could get shopped around if the Thunder look light on the wings following their summer subtractions.

Should the Magic learn that the hiring of head coach Sean Sweeney wasn't enough to lift this group's first-round ceiling, then some wildly interesting names could hit the rumor mill.

For now, though, Orlando's focus should be strengthening the supporting cast around its costly core . If the Magic feel less than fully confident in their shooting and wing depth, they could flip Bitadze for a more obvious need-filler.

Bitadze is a solid backup big, but Orlando could be fine in that role without him after Nikola Vučević's return and the addition of rookie second-rounder Izaiyah Nelson.

The Sixers are clearly going for it after adding both Jaylen Brown and LeBron James this offseason to team with Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey. They'll give this roster every chance to succeed until it proves that it cannot.

They have as much star power as anyone in the Association, so if they seek help on the trade market, they'll merely shop for support players. And they might already have a pressing need there after reserve center Ariel Hukporti suffered a torn Achilles.

If they think covering that role is mission-critical, then they could sacrifice some wing depth to do it. Edwards, who barely averaged half as many minutes last season (15.3) as he did as a rookie (26.3), is a theoretical three-and-D wing, but he isn't guaranteed to deliver with either aspect of that role.

There are a lot of different ways to imagine how the ideal co-star for Devin Booker would play. None of them remotely resemble Green.

Sure, when his three-ball is hitting, and his explosiveness is leaping off the screen, he seems like a star in the making. But even then, he isn't the passer, creator or consistent shooter you'd want alongside Booker in the backcourt.

Green might ultimately work best as an off-the-bench spark plug, but the Suns can't really use him as such when he is their second-highest-paid player and might have their second-deepest offensive bag (which says more about his teammates' limitations than anything).

Portland's four-headed monster at point guard feels like the NBA's embodiment of the One's Gotta Go game. The Blazers have expressed confidence in their guard-heavy roster, but that's really their lone hope to avoid losing all leverage in trade talks.

There just isn't a great basketball way to slot Holiday, Damian Lillard, Ja Morant and Scoot Henderson into the same rotation. Especially when 2025-26 All-Star Deni Avdija needs plenty of touches, too. Things will only grow more crowded once Shaedon Sharpe returns from a meniscus tear.

If Portland needs to subtract a perimeter player, Holiday might offer the best blend of trade value and replaceability. Lillard and Morant have questionable value given their recent availability issues, and Henderson's stock seems too low to sell. Holiday should have ample appeal to win-now shoppers, and the Blazers have enough stoppers to get by without his defensive versatility.

The Kings have a few veterans who could easily appear here, but Sabonis has the best shot of actually bringing back something (or someone) of substance.

Sacramento wouldn't fetch a blank-check type of return for the three-time All-Star. There are gaps in his game at both ends of the floor, and he has the reputation of raising a regular-season floor but lowering a postseason ceiling. That said, he is an elite rebounder, an elite passer for a center and a true stat sheet-stuffer, so the right, offense-needy club could part with a real asset or two to get him.

And as an added bonus, getting rid of Sabonis might mean clearing Maxime Raynaud, an All-Rookie second-teamer last season, for take-off.

The Spurs re-signed Barnes this summer, and he took a big paycut to stay, so there is obviously a mutual appreciation of the other. His appearance here, then, is more about the lack of obvious alternatives.

We could have gotten bold and put De'Aaron Fox, but we don't actually believe it. Not yet, anyway. As talented as San Antonio's young guards are, Fox is still the best option for organizing and running an offense.

So, it's sort of Barnes by default. His experience and willingness to stay within his role are helpful to have, but a forward rotation featuring Devin Vassell, Julian Champagnie, Keldon Johnson, Carter Bryant and Tobias Harris could easily get by without him.

This is, admittedly, an easier-said-than-done response. If Toronto had a taker for Poeltl—and the three-year, $84.1 million extension he won't start until next season—he would've had a new hoops home by now.

It's still worth (repeatedly) working the phones to try getting something done. Because with Kawhi Leonard back north of the border, the Raptors might be just an upgrade at center away from contending for the Eastern Conference crown.

The Leonard-Scottie Barnes tandem should be one of basketball's best forward combos. An Immanuel Quickley-RJ Barrett backcourt is more than adequate. And this bench had a top-10 net rating last season. The other puzzle pieces might all be in place, but the Raptors need a more reliable and dynamic option at center to complete the picture.

Care to guess how many players on the Jazz will make more money than Green this season? Here's a hint: It's a much smaller number than the amount of players likely to log more minutes than him.

The answer is two: Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen. Everyone else is making less than Green's $14.7 million (expiring) salary , which isn't an egregious amount by NBA standards but could easily read that way if he isn't part of the regular rotation.

He isn't guaranteed to be a locked-in piece of the nightly plans. He sort of fits the three-and-D label, but Utah could turn different directions to address those needs, getting more defense from Josh Okogie and more shooting out of Svi Mykhailiuk. Tack on sparky scorer Brice Sensabaugh and whichever prized prospect gets squeezed out of the starting five (Darryn Peterson or Ace Bailey), and that's a healthy wing reserve unit without a nearly $15 million Green.

This might be the least fun slide to write, because the best-case-scenario season for the reworked Wizards could be all kinds of fun. But does a team with this much youth really want to lock itself into a major-money arrangement with an oft-injured 33-year-old? It certainly should not.

"There's almost no chance the Wizards will give him that max extension—not with his injury history, not at his age, not with the team in this stage of its development and the punitive first and second aprons looming," The Athletic's David Aldridge and Josh Robbins wrote. "Even as the team has said repeatedly that acquiring Davis and point guard Trae Young through trades earlier this year was done to help Washington begin to compete and try to win games after three years of tanking, the Wizards' future ... still revolves around its young core group, led now by AJ Dybantsa, the first pick in this year's draft."

Washington already overpaid Young to stick around, but at least he is young enough (28) to pilot this offense for a while and generally reliable to hit the hardwood. Doubling down with anything close to a max deal for Davis would wreck the Wizards' cap sheet, making it drastically more difficult to keep all of this young talent it has collected. Better to find a taker for Davis now and let someone else calculate his next contract.

articles.title: LeBron James' Wildest Endorsement Deals and Investments
articles.summary: LeBron James' path to becoming one of the greatest NBA players ever is built on unseen hours of training, exercise, skill development and so much more.
articles.body:
LeBron James' path to becoming one of the greatest NBA players ever is built on unseen hours of training, exercise, skill development and so much more.

Not only did "The King" become the first NBA player ever to surpass $500 million in career salary, but he's also banked many millions in off-court earnings. Much of this additional income is through endorsement deals and savvy investments.

Here, we've highlighted some of the most notable off-court deals that helped LeBron reach an estimated net worth of $1.4 billion .

Since joining the Philadelphia 76ers, LeBron's most recent endorsement deal—as of this writing—is from Polymarket. According to Front Office Sports , the contract is worth $15 million annually.

To put that into context, he'll earn almost four times as much from Polymarket this year as he does from the Sixers.

James reportedly will not be promoting basketball and instead will focus on football for the prediction market platform.

Prior to his endorsement with Polymarket, LeBron served as a brand ambassador for gambling entity DraftKings Sportsbook. The dollar figure was unreported , but it lasted from early 2024 into the summer of 2026.

James occasionally shared NFL picks and appeared in several commercials with comedian Kevin Hart for the company.

Back in 2024, LeBron inked a partnership with Fanatics after a 20-year run at trading card rival Upper Deck.

Complete terms of this contract are unavailable, though experts cited by CNBC estimated it could be worth more than $5 million per year.

Front Office Sports later reported the agreement includes usage of the company's aviation, which has come in handy for LeBron's helicopter travels from his New York City home to Philadelphia for work.

10 Most All-Time Expensive Sports Jersey Sales💰

Players With the Most to Prove This Season 🏀

In connection with longtime friend and business partner Maverick Carter, LeBron has made several shrewd investments as well.

Carter, LeBron and financial adviser Paul Wachter put less than $1 million in Blaze Pizza back in 2012. Five years later, James' approximate 10 percent ownership in the company was worth $25 million, as ESPN's Darren Rovell reported at the time.

Rovell also noted that endorsement payments pushed LeBron's stake in the business toward the $35-40 million range.

During his memorable run on the Miami Heat as part of a "Big Three" alongside Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh, LeBron cashed a nice off-court check.

Apple purchased Beats Electronics for $3 billion, and ESPN's Brian Windhorst and Marc Stein reported that James received $30 million in profit as part of the sale. They added that it was "believed to be the biggest equity cash payout for a professional athlete in history" at the time.

LeBron received an initial stake in the company in 2008 as part of an agreement to promote the Beats by Dre headphones.

SpringHill Company: $725 Million Valuation

Named as a nod to the housing complex in which he was raised, James established the SpringHill Company alongside Carter with roots back to 2007.

SpringHill has produced some notable TV series and films, including James as the star in Space Jam: A New Legacy . Others include NBC game show The Wall , HBO talk show The Shop and Netflix docuseries The Playbook .

In a 2021 minority stake sale, SpringHill had a $725 million valuation. Variety reported James and Carter maintained controlling interest in the company.

While playing for the Heat in 2011, LeBron acquired a minority interest in Liverpool Football Club as part of an agreement with Fenway Sports Group that granted the company exclusive rights to marketing his image.

ESPN's Darren Rovell reported in 2018 that his 2 percent stake—initially worth $6.5 million—had turned into a $32 million valuation.

According to Joe Vardon and Mike Vorkunov of The Athletic , James joined FSG as a partner in 2021 with a 1 percent stake and, alongside Carter, received more equity in the firm in 2023. In addition to the Premier League club, FSG properties include the Boston Red Sox (MLB), Pittsburgh Penguins (NHL) and RFK Racing (NASCAR).

Before he ever stepped foot on an NBA court—even before his name was called first overall in the 2003 draft—LeBron had achieved generational wealth.

The kid from Akron, Ohio, signed a seven-year contract worth $90-plus million with apparel giant Nike. The deal included a $10 million signing bonus as James passed up offers from Adidas and Reebok.

LeBron's first endorsement deal with Nike gave him life-changing money. The second, signed in 2010, locked him in as a longtime brand ambassador. The third ensured his legacy would always be tied to Nike.

Nike signed him to a lifetime deal in 2015, and ESPN's Darren Rovell reported that it included "the largest single-athlete guarantee in company history."

In a 2016 interview with GQ , LeBron's business partner, Maverick Carter, pointed "one finger skyward" after the interviewer asked whether the contract was worth $1 billion.

articles.title: Bronny James, Luka Doncic's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights from Lakers vs. Kings Preseason
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers improved their preseason record to 2-1 on Thursday night thanks to a 114-110 victory over the Sacramento Kings.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers improved their preseason record to 2-1 on Thursday night thanks to a 114-110 victory over the Sacramento Kings.

Luka Dončić's 23 points led all players. Bronny James did a little bit of everything in his 22 minutes off the bench for head coach JJ Redick.

One thing Dončić has struggled to get going thus far is his shooting touch. He made just six of his 16 field-goal attempts against the Kings and is 11-of-28 in two preseason contest thus far.

Even when Dončić's shot isn't working overall, there are still incredible moments overall. He tossed up a three from close to the logo to beat the shot clock and it went in.

These are minor issues because Dončić is one of the most efficient scorers in the NBA. He also got to the free-throw line nine times without a miss, so even his poor shooting nights won't keep him from putting up a lot of points.

James' efficiency does remain a concern to keep an eye on. He only attempted three shots, making one, so the sample size against the Kings isn't robust.

However, the 22-year-old is shooting 30.8 percent overall in three preseason contests. It is his best preseason field-goal percentage, up from 29.7 percent during his rookie year and 25.7 last season, but you would hope for more improvement if he is going to turn into a notable contributor in the regular season.

One encouraging sign from James was his playmaking and passing. He dished out six assists in his 22 minutes and is averaging 4.3 per game in the preseason.

The Lakers need to make up for some loss in playmaking with LeBron James no longer on the roster. Dončić and Austin Reaves will get the bulk of the responsibility, but James could play himself into more minutes as a ball-handler when they are off the floor.

Los Angeles will get four days off before returning to action on Oct. 13 against the Golden State Warriors from T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.

articles.title: Vivek Ranadive Reportedly Called Out Kings Players, Staff with 'Roast' at Team Dinner
articles.summary: Sacramento King governor Vivek Ranadivé reportedly employed a unique motivational tactic at a recent team dinner.
articles.body:
Sacramento King governor Vivek Ranadivé reportedly employed a unique motivational tactic at a recent team dinner.

Speaking Thursday on the Zach Lowe Show (h/t NBABase ), The Ringer's Zach Lowe reported that Ranadivé roasted his entire team, including players and staff members.

"They went out to a fancy training [camp] dinner, team, the whole team, the staff, everything," Lowe said. "And at the dinner, Vivek Ranadivé spoke, and he kind of turned the dinner into a roast of lots of people in the room, telling them all the ways in which they have been failing as players, coaches, executives, whatever."

LeBron rejects rumor he yelled at new teammate

Broadcaster sorry for false LeBron rumor

Lowe added, "Some people were alarmed and were like, 'This is not going over the way you intended.' Some people thought, 'I get what he's doing, he's using the fact that we've become a media punch line to motivate us.' He was not saying, 'I, Vivek Ranadivé, believe these things about you, but here's what people say about you, prove us wrong.'"

Ranadivé purchased the Kings in 2013, and he has not presided over much success since then.

In fact, the Kings have made the playoffs only one time during Ranadivé's tenure, that being a first-round exit at the hands of the Golden State Warriors in 2023.

There was hope that the Kings had finally gotten out of the doldrums at that point, as they ended a 16-year playoff drought, but it did not prove to be the momentum builder many expected.

Instead, the Kings narrowly missed the playoffs with a 46-36 record in 2024, dipped to 40-42 in 2025, and bottomed out last season with a 22-60 mark, which was tied for the worst record in the Western Conference.

Throughout the offseason, rumors and speculation ran rampant regarding the Kings having a fire sale and moving on from many of their best players.

Sacramento did waive DeMar DeRozan, but the likes of Domantas Sabonis and Zach LaVine are somewhat surprisingly still on the roster.

Perhaps the Kings want to see if they can mesh well with rookie No. 7 overall draft pick Darius Acuff Jr., catch lightning in a bottle and get the team back in the playoff mix.

If not, both Sabonis and LaVine will undoubtedly be popular trade candidates throughout the 2026-27 campaign.

The first opportunity to see if Ranadivé's motivational tactics worked will come on Oct. 21 when the Kings go on the road to face the Los Angeles Clippers in their regular-season opener.

articles.title: Knicks Pause Contract Talks with KAT, Josh Hart, Deuce McBride to Focus on Prep for NBA Season
articles.summary: The New York Knicks announced Friday that they are pausing all contract negotiations as they prepare for the start of the 2026-27 NBA regular season.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks announced Friday that they are pausing all contract negotiations as they prepare for the start of the 2026-27 NBA regular season.

In a statement provided to ESPN's Shams Charania , the Knicks said, "As an organization, our entire focus is on preparing for the upcoming season and delivering another year for our fans to be proud of. As a result, we will not be negotiating contract extensions until later in the season and will remain solely focused on preparing for the start of the season."

Per ESPN's Bobby Marks , the likes of Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart, Miles McBride and Tyler Kolek are all extension eligible, and the Knicks have until June 30 to get deals done with them.

The Knicks are coming off their first championship-winning season since 1973, as they ran roughshod over the playoffs, going 16-3 during the postseason.

Towns and Hart were especially big contributors to the title with KAT averaging 15.9 points, 10.6 rebounds and 4.9 assists per game during the playoffs to go along with Hart's 10.4 points, 8.9 rebounds and 4.6 assists per contest.

McBride and Kolek weren't used quite as heavily come playoff time, but McBride averaged a career-high 12.0 points per game as a key bench player during the 2025-26 regular season, while Kolek also set career highs with 4.4 points and 2.7 assists per game.

The 30-year-old Towns is the biggest name on the Knicks roster who could become a free agent next offseason, provided he declines his player option.

Originally selected first overall by the Minnesota Timberwolves in the 2015 NBA draft, Towns is a six-time All-Star and three-time All-NBA selection who has averaged 22.2 points, 12.3 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game over his two seasons in New York.

Fred Katz of The Athletic reported last week that the Knicks want to pay Towns "much less" than the four-year, $276 million extension he is eligible to sign.

Last week on NBA Today , ESPN's Malika Andrews reported that although Towns is "willing to take a pay cut," he believes the Knicks' current offer is "unreasonable."

According to Charania , the Knicks' most recent offer to Towns was worth about $200 million over four years.

There is a team option in Hart's contract for the 2027-28 campaign, so there may not be as much of a sense of urgency to extend him as Towns.

Still, Hart is a hugely important player for the Knicks, as he contributes a little bit of everything as the Swiss army knife of the starting lineup.

The 31-year-old veteran averaged 12.0 points, 7.4 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game last season, providing support to the likes of Towns, Jalen Brunson, OG Anunoby and Mikal Bridges.

One can only assume the Knicks may want to revisit things at some point, especially when it comes to Towns, but for now they are focused on getting ready for the regular-season opener against the Philadelphia 76ers on Oct. 20.

articles.title: El Valencia Basket sigue en la cumbre: una reconstrucción obligada para que nada cambie
articles.standfirst: Los taronjas, con nueve fichajes y nuevo técnico, inician la era post Pedro Martínez igualando su mejor arranque en Euroliga (4-0) y son los únicos que aguantan el ritmo del Panathinaikos
articles.summary: Los taronjas, con nueve fichajes y nuevo técnico, inician la era post Pedro Martínez igualando su mejor arranque en Euroliga (4-0) y son los únicos que aguantan el ritmo del Panathinaikos
articles.body: Han cambiado los jugadores, con nueve fichajes, y ha cambiado el entrenador, Xavi Albert, pero el Valencia Basket no parece haber cambiado. Como si una temporada se hubiera juntado con otra, terminó la anterior siendo un equipo admirado disputando su primera Final Four y ha comenzado la actual como una de las grandes sensaciones: invicto colíder junto al transatlántico Panathinaikos. Nadie le sacará de la segunda plaza cuando acabe esta cuarta jornada. Su 4-0 que figura en la clasificación lo ha conseguido con el mismo juego atractivo y ritmo vertiginoso del curso pasado. Promedia más de 100 puntos por noche: 96 en el estreno contra el Besiktas, 111 al Kosner Baskonia, 105 en la visita al ASVEL con gran remontada incluida y 93 para tumbar al Hapoel Tel Aviv. Y todos los efectivos aportando pese a que nadie juega más de 24 minutos. En los cuatro encuentros han anotado un mínimo de 10 jugadores. "Es una muestra muy pequeña en una temporada extraordinariamente larga. Estoy muy contento porque veo cada día al equipo mejor y si lo veo en los días en los que caigamos será lo que más contento me pondrá", analizaba Xavi Albert tras sumar el póker de victorias e igualar el mejor arranque taronja en su historia en la máxima competición continental. Imposible encontrar una mejor manera de disipar las razonables dudas tras la obligada reconstrucción acometida en verano. Los taronjas perdieron a jugadores fundamentales como Jean Montero, Jaime Pradilla, Brancou Badio, Braxton Key... Y, sobre todo, vieron marchar al ideólogo de todo aquello, Pedro Martínez. Tuvieron que cambiar todo para que nada cambiara: misma filosofía y, por ahora, mismos resultados. Excelentes. A los mandos, TJ Shorts, que ha encontrado en Valencia la libertad que tuvo en París y no disfrutó en el Panathinaikos con Ergin Ataman. Como hombre para todo, delante y detrás, Kameron Taylor, la única estrella que se quedó. Con el capitán Josep Puerto acertadísimo desde el triple. Y disfrutando de Nikola Mirotic, leyenda de la Euroliga que llegaba como guinda del pastel y se ha convertido en uno de los ingredientes principales. Un club, un equipo y un juego que despierta incluso la admiración de los rivales. "El Valencia jugó la Final Four y ganó la Liga ACB. Fue una temporada sensacional para ellos y aunque ha cambiado mucho, mantiene la filosofía y ese crecimiento llega con una dinámica con el club, con el nuevo pabellón y la afición y eso hace que pueda ser imparable", comentaba Dimitris Itoudis, entrenador del Hapoel, tras perder en el Roig Arena. La próxima semana, en el inicio de una nueva doble jornada, prueba definitiva en la visita del campeón Olympiacos con Sasha Vezenkov, Nikola Milutinov y el antiguo ídolo Jean Montero al frente.

articles.title: Joel Embiid Calls Rumor About LeBron James Practice Spat 'Not True,' Says He's 'Easy Target'
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Joel Embiid has dismissed the rumor of a practice spat between him and LeBron James.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star Joel Embiid has dismissed the rumor of a practice spat between him and LeBron James.

Following the Sixers' preseason game against the Brooklyn Nets, Embiid told reporters the rumor is "not true" and he's not sure where it came from beyond him being an "easy target" given his history.

"It sucks, but what can you do? It's unfortunate. I don't know where that came from. It never happened. ... I think we just got to focus on ourselves. There's going to be a lot of outside noise to pull us apart from what we're supposed to be and what we're supposed to accomplish. So, it's important that we stay together and we keep our [head] down. ... Those type of things, I can't understand. One, it is not true, but then again, it's like, 'Why me?' ... I guess I'm Joel Embiid. I've been in that situation. I don't usually talk when it comes to those [rumors]. So, it feels like I'm an easy target. But yeah, as long as we know who we are [we will be OK] and we just got to stick together."

The situation began on Monday during the Sixers' preseason contest with the New York Knicks. Play-by-play announcer Mike Breen, who was calling the game on MSG Networks, said he heard a story in which James left Embiid "have it" for walking out late for practice.

"Somebody told me before the game that they were out ready to practice and Joel Embiid walked out on the court a couple of minutes late, and LeBron let him hear it," Breen said on the broadcast (h/t Tyler Lauletta of Awful Announcing).

Embiid is not the only member of the Sixers organization who has disputed the story. James wrote "stop the lies" on his Instagram Story, adding Embiid has not been late for any practice.

76ers head coach Nick Nurse told reporters on Wednesday he was "surprised" when he heard about Breen's comments because Embiid is "in great shape; he's been on the practice floor."

Amid the pushback, Breen issued an apology, which was relayed by ESPN's Dave McMenamin : "I don't know why the person who told me the story would make it up, but if LeBron says it never happened then I believe him and apologize for putting it out there."

Breen added he got the story from "someone I trust" and only thought of it as an "interesting anecdote" to show how James is having a positive influence with his new team, but it took off in a way he didn't anticipate.

"For me, the fact that the teammate was Joel was meaningless," he said. "In hindsight, I should have realized the fact that it was Joel is what made it a story. I've always been a huge fan of Joel and feel awful that it put the focus on him the way that it did."

James and Embiid made their preseason debuts for the 76ers on Thursday night. Embiid finished with six points and eight turnovers in 24 minutes. James had 10 points on 8-of-8 free-throw shooting in 18 minutes.

The Sixers have two more preseason games remaining before tipping off the regular season against the defending NBA champion New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on Oct. 20.

articles.title: "Women helping women turn their passions into a livelihood": How Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry helped two sisters with a $100,000 doll business that sold fewer than 100
articles.summary: A $100,000 investment should give a business a strong start, but Carlissa and Laken King soon faced a difficult reality.
articles.body: A $100,000 investment should give a business a strong start, but Carlissa and Laken King soon faced a difficult reality. The twin sisters had spent that amount manufacturing 3,000 dolls for Worldgirls, their inclusive doll company, yet they had sold fewer than 100. They needed more than a good product to reach customers. In 2019, Stephen Curry’s wife, Ayesha Curry, stepped in through Fempire, her series for female entrepreneurs, offering the sisters connections and opportunities to help them build their brand.Ayesha did not simply offer encouraging words. She connected the sisters with people who could help them understand their audience, improve their branding and find new ways to sell their dolls. Her support opened doors to major retail opportunities, including QVC and the American International Toy Fair. However, the sisters’ experience also showed that business growth takes more than one big break.How Ayesha Curry helped Worldgirls after its $100,000 investment struggled to pay offWhen Carlissa and Laken King appeared on Fempire, which premiered on EllenTube in Nov. 2019, their business needed a clearer direction. They had invested $100,000 to manufacture 3,000 dolls but had not sold even 100. The problem was not simply making the dolls. They needed to reach the right customers and help people understand their brand.Ayesha Curry wanted to help entrepreneurs turn their ideas into sustainable businesses. In her Dec. 27, 2019, interview with Forbes, she described the purpose of her series, saying, “Fempire is women helping women turn their passions into a livelihood.” She also explained, “A great idea unfortunately doesn’t always equate to a successful business.”Ayesha put that approach into practice with the King sisters. She introduced them to Lauren Auslander, CEO of public relations firm LUNA. Auslander helped them define their target audience and refine their brand.Ayesha also helped the sisters secure a booth at the 2020 American International Toy Fair in New York City. She arranged an appearance on QVC and meetings with five toy stores. These opportunities gave Worldgirls more chances to introduce its inclusive dolls to retailers and potential customers.The support offered something the sisters had struggled to gain on their own: access to people who could help them grow. Still, getting noticed did not guarantee sales, and the sisters remained aware of the work ahead. Why the Worldgirls founders said building their brand was no quick fixDespite the new opportunities, the sisters did not pretend that Ayesha’s help had solved every problem. In the profile, Laken King explained that the business continued to struggle with visibility.“Even after all of the exposure, it’s been really hard to gain that visibility,” Laken told.She then offered the line that captures the reality behind their experience: “It’s not a miracle, it’s not a magic pill.” Laken explained that one of Ayesha’s most useful lessons was to keep going because building a business and creating brand awareness takes time.The sisters’ experience showed that manufacturing 3,000 dolls was only the first step. Reaching customers required a separate effort. The Toy Fair booth, QVC appearance and toy-store meetings created opportunities, but they did not guarantee sales.Ayesha’s own experience helped explain why she wanted to support women like the King sisters.
