articles.title: Knicks suspend contract extension talks for Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart 'until later in the season'
articles.summary: On the eve of a new season, the Knicks have tabled negotiations with extension-eligible players — including two key starters from last year's title team.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks announced Friday they are suspending all negotiations on contract extensions with eligible players — including Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart, key starters on the team that won the NBA championship in June — until "later in the season."

"As an organization, our entire focus is on preparing for the upcoming season and delivering another year for our fans to be proud of," a Knicks spokesperson said in a statement issued to multiple news outlets Friday. "As a result, we will not be negotiating contract extensions until later in the season and will remain solely focused on preparing for the start of the season."

Towns, Hart, sixth man Miles "Deuce" McBride and reserve point guard Tyler Kolek are all eligible for extensions of their current contracts. Towns, who holds a $61 million player option for 2027-28 campaign, is eligible for an extension worth a maximum of $276 million over four years. Hart, whose deal includes a $22.4 million team option for 2027-28, can extend for up to $132 million over four years.

McBride, now entering the final year of the three-year, $13 million extension he signed in 2023 , is slated to reach unrestricted free agency this summer. Kolek, a second-round pick out of Marquette in 2024, has a $2.5 million team option for 2027-28.

After spending the summer celebrating their remarkable domination of the Eastern Conference and five-game victory over the San Antonio Spurs in the 2026 NBA Finals, the honeymoon following the franchise's first title in 53 years appeared to end on media day last month, when it became clear that a lack of progress in extension talks was a paramount concern for Towns, the All-Star center who played perhaps the best basketball of his life during the Knicks' run to the championship, and Hart, whose relentlessness so often fueled New York's best moments , heading into the new season.

The deadline for the Knicks to reach extension agreements with all four eligible players doesn't come until June 30, 2027 — meaning they can ink new deals at any point throughout this season. To do it in-season, though, the player must be on an expiring contract ; this means that Towns would have to decline his player option for 2027-28, and the Knicks would have to decline their team options on Hart and Kolek.

For the players, though, the prospect of putting discussions on the back-burner rather than getting them squared away before the start of the season can represent a somewhat disquieting risk.

"You always want to get it done, kind of as soon as possible, obviously, because you don't want that trickling into the season," Hart said on media day. "Because whenever there's uncertainty, there's gonna be a lot of questions, there's gonna be a lot of rumors. At a human level, sometimes that can wear people down, and it can affect how you go out and handle business on a day-to-day basis, just some of that uncertainty."

Towns underscored his discomfort with that uncertainty before New York's preseason opener against the Philadelphia 76ers on Monday.

"Simply put, I want to do something to keep the team together and can work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns told reporters. "And none of those things are close to happening."

Why those things aren't close to happening — for Towns specifically, and for the other extension-eligible Knicks in general — likely relates to New York's concerns about steering clear of the second apron in the years to come.

As it stands, New York has just under $226.7 million in salary committed on the books for the 2027-28 season, according to Spotrac — about $9.3 million below the projected second apron line for that season. That figure includes team options on Hart, Kolek and 2024 first-round pick Pacôme Dadiet, and does not include a new deal for McBride.

The second apron line is critical because, just four days after the Knicks beat the Spurs, owner James L. Dolan went on New York radio station WFAN and made it clear that he did not intend to approve an offseason spending plan that would increase the team's total salary commitments for this season past that second-apron threshold.

Dolan called the prospect of spending into the second apron something "that you'd have to be, you know, suicidal to do." Crossing that line not only imposes a higher tax rate on high-spending teams, but also strips away team-building and roster-management tools like access to salary-cap exceptions, the ability to aggregate players' salaries in trades, the option of sending cash to another team to grease the skids on a swap, and the freedom to acquire players in sign-and-trade deals, among other restrictions.

Dolan's radio-appearance edict reportedly "blindsided" the Knicks front office, which wanted to go over the second apron after patiently and meticulously building a championship roster . Instead, New York spent its summer maneuvering to stay below that $222 million line — and, in the process, lost backup center Mitchell Robinson, who signed a three-year, $47.4 million deal with the Boston Celtics.

The Knicks don't have to stay below the second apron; in fact, it's reasonable to argue that, as a confirmed championship-level team squarely in the middle of its contending window, they are precisely the sort of team that can and should be willing to go above that line for at least one season. They are, as SNY's Ian Begley put it , "voluntarily limited" by Dolan's public and apparently ongoing insistence that he will not authorize such spending. Amid the ongoing rancor surrounding Towns' contract talks, Friday's statement pausing all extension negotiations suggests that the owner's tune isn't changing anytime soon.

It's unclear whether Dolan's "stay below the second apron" mandate will apply past this season, stretching out to 2027-28, 2028-29 and beyond. If it does, though, it becomes exceedingly difficult to envision a scenario in which the Knicks — who will also see Jalen Brunson and OG Anunoby become extension-eligible next summer — keep together the core that just won the championship. The math essentially demands significant financial sacrifice, beyond even the cost savings that New York was able to realize when Brunson opted to extend a year ahead of free agency and when Anunoby and Mikal Bridges took slightly less than their maximum salaries in their respective re-ups.

Towns now finds himself at the center of that "sacrifice for the good of the roster vs. advocate to earn your market rate" conflict. The Knicks have reportedly offered Towns a four-year, $200 million extension — less than he got from the Timberwolves in 2022 and more than $75 million below his max. Towns clearly does not feel that offer accurately reflects the contributions he's made since arriving in New York before the start of the 2024-25 season.

Asked on Monday whether he felt he deserved to be rewarded for that level of achievement on his next deal, Towns told reporters : "No s***, Sherlock. I just won a championship. You'd think it was pretty easy. Unless you guys think I have something else to prove."

Whether Dolan, Knicks team president Leon Rose or someone else in New York's decision-making apparatus thinks Towns, Hart and Co. still have something to prove to earn their next pact, or they're just trying to both play hardball in negotiations in an effort to squeeze under that owner-imposing spending cap, the Knicks have made it clear that they are — for now, at least — done talking terms.

It's unclear at what point "later in the season" they might change their mind and be willing to come back to the table. For now, the Knicks, who'd been hoping to settle their business before the season, will have to just deal with the uncertainty and hope to play their way into a big payday — and the rest of the team, and its fan base, will have to hope that the ambient frustration and unpleasantness surrounding all this doesn't leach into the Knicks' efforts to defend their title.

"At the end of the day, we're humans, and I think what sometimes gets lost is that we are people — that we all have lives and things that we have to deal with and fix," Hart said on media day. "I wish I could sit there and say it wouldn't have any weight or any bearing, but you never know. Some people can handle it great, and some people can really struggle with it and that can kill their performance. I hope it gets done, but we'll see."

articles.title: New NBA Rumors on Pistons' Kevin Durant, Kawhi Leonard Trade Pursuits in Free Agency
articles.summary: Before finally resolving their contract standoff with Jalen Duren, the Detroit Pistons were trying to make a huge splash in the trade market this offseason to upgrade their roster around Cade Cunningham.
articles.body:
Before finally resolving their contract standoff with Jalen Duren, the Detroit Pistons were trying to make a huge splash in the trade market this offseason to upgrade their roster around Cade Cunningham.

Per ESPN's Vincent Goodwill , the Pistons made trade inquiries for Kevin Durant and Kawhi Leonard over the summer.

It doesn't sound like Detroit's attempts ever went very far with Goodwill noting Leonard "wasn't interested" in playing for the Pistons and the Houston Rockets "weren't willing to engage" in talks for Durant.

Durant has had high praise for Cunningham throughout his career. The future Hall of Famer called the Pistons star a "special" talent.

Cunningham led the Pistons to 60 wins and the No. 1 seed in the Eastern Conference last season, but they struggled through the first two rounds of the playoffs before being eliminated in by the Cleveland Cavaliers in the conference semifinals.

The loss opened up concerns about how good the supporting cast around Cunningham was, with Duren being the biggest question mark because he had been so effective in the regular season to earn a spot on the All-NBA third team.

Duren averaged 10.2 points and 8.5 rebounds per game in 14 postseason starts. He put up 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds per contest in 70 starts during the regular season.

The slump for Duren led to a prolonged contract negotiation with the Pistons that finally got resolved on Monday when he agreed to a five-year, $200 million deal.

Duren's contract ensures he and Cunningham will be the primary pieces in Detroit for the foreseeable future. The duo will account for more than $90 million in salary over each of the next four seasons.

There is still room for growth with Duren since he is only 22. Still, it's hard not to wonder what a Pistons roster with Leonard or Durant playing next to Cunningham might have looked like.

articles.title: Jalen Duren Reportedly Was Called '4th-Best' Pistons Player During $200M Contract Talks
articles.summary: Before signing a five-year, $200 million contract with the Detroit Pistons last week, All-Star center Jalen Duren reportedly took issue with how he was being characterized during negotiations.
articles.body:
Before signing a five-year, $200 million contract with the Detroit Pistons last week, All-Star center Jalen Duren reportedly took issue with how he was being characterized during negotiations.

According to ESPN's Vincent Goodwill , Duren was frustrated to hear himself referred to as the Pistons' "fourth-best player" during contract talks.

Selected 13th overall in the 2022 NBA draft, Duren has been an impact player for the Pistons throughout his four-year career.

He took his game to the next level last season, though, averaging a career-high 19.5 points per game on 65.0 percent shooting to go along with 10.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists.

As a result, Duren was named an All-Star for the first time in addition to being an All-NBA Third Team selection.

With Duren and guard Cade Cunningham leading the way, the Pistons shockingly posted the best record in the Eastern Conference last season at 60-22, making them arguably the team to beat in the playoffs.

Detroit survived a tough challenge from the eighth-seeded Orlando Magic in the first round, beating them in seven games, but the Pistons then fell in seven games to the Cleveland Cavaliers in the second round.

Duren's significant dip in play from the regular season to the postseason was a major talking point after the Pistons were eliminated, as he averaged just 10.2 points on 51.4 percent shooting, plus 8.5 rebounds and 2.1 assists in 14 playoff games.

He especially struggled with 9.9 points, 7.6 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game during the second round.

Duren was clearly the Pistons' second-best player during the regular season behind only Cunningham, but in the playoffs, he was their fourth-leading scorer behind Cunningham, Tobias Harris and Duncan Robinson.

Despite that and any hurt feelings that may have come from the negotiations, Duren and the Pistons got on the same page and agreed to a new deal, meaning he will be counted upon to be a key player for the team once again this coming season and beyond.

articles.title: Ilusionante estreno de De Larrea en los Mavericks con Durant enfrente
articles.standfirst: El base español hace 11 puntos con tres triples sin fallo y seis asistencias en la derrota de su equipo ante los Rockets en Macao (117-135)
articles.summary: El base español hace 11 puntos con tres triples sin fallo y seis asistencias en la derrota de su equipo ante los Rockets en Macao (117-135)
articles.body: Sergio De Larrea se enfundó la camiseta de los Mavericks para disputar su primer partido. Aunque tuvo poco de normalidad. Al comienzo de la pretemporada, con ausencias, entre un sinfín de rotaciones, en Macao... El base español dejó buenas sensaciones en la derrota de su equipo ante los Rockets por 117-135. El joven jugador vallisoletano (20 años) se estrenó con 11 puntos, con 4/6 en tiros de campo incluidos tres triples sin fallo, seis asistencias, dos rebotes y una recuperación en 24 minutos en pista. Lo peor de su estadística, cuatro pérdidas. Mientras él estuvo en la cancha, su equipo perdió por tres. Buena imagen para quien fuera elegido en el puesto 25 del último draft por los Lakers, aunque posteriormente fue enviado a los Knicks y finalmente recaló en Dallas. Kyrie Irving debería estar listo para el inicio de la temporada regular tras superar una grave lesión de rodilla, pero no jugó ante los Rockets. Tampoco el otro español de los Mavericks, Santi Aldama. El mejor del equipo fue Cooper Flagg, que debería confirmarse como una gran estrella de la NBA después de ser el último rookie del año. Sumó 19 puntos en otros tantos minutos y añadió seis rebotes. Naji Marshall, con 16 puntos, y Max Christie, con 14, fueron otros de los Mavericks que destacaron en ataque en el Venetian Arena de Macao. Hasta 14 jugadores alineó Dusty May, el entrenador que ha sustituido a Jason Kidd en el banquillo. Ya tiene experiencia con españoles. Fue el técnico que dirigió a Aday Mara en la Universidad de Míchigan, a la que llevó al título universitario la temporada pasada. En los Rockets, un Kevin Durant a medio gas se quedó en 15 puntos mientras que el turco Alperen Sengun hizo un triple-doble con 16+10+10, Tari Eason fue el mejor anotador del encuentro con 20 puntos saliendo desde el banquillo y Fred VanVleet, que volvió a jugar 523 días después de romperse el ligamento cruzado anterior de la rodilla derecha, puso la dirección con 17 y siete asistencias.

articles.title: New Kyrie Irving Trade Rumors on Pistons' Interest in Pairing Alongside Cade Cunningham
articles.summary: The Detroit Pistons reportedly could have their sights set on adding a dynamic and accomplished guard to play alongside Cade Cunningham.
articles.body:
The Detroit Pistons reportedly could have their sights set on adding a dynamic and accomplished guard to play alongside Cade Cunningham.

According to ESPN's Vincent Goodwill , multiple Pistons staffers are "fond" of Dallas Mavericks star Kyrie Irving's "game, shot creation and malleability," particularly while teaming with fellow star players such as LeBron James and Luka Dončić.

Irving, 34, missed the entire 2025-26 season while recovering from a torn ACL, and the 2026-27 campaign could be his final year under contract, as he has a player option for 2027-28.

Because of that, the Mavs could conceivably look to move Irving prior to the 2026-27 trade deadline if they aren't showing marked improvement from the 26-56 record they posted last season.

Detroit would potentially be an excellent fit for Kyrie due to the possibility of contending for a championship with the Pistons, while teaming up with a pair of All-Stars in Cunningham and Jalen Duren.

A nine-time All-Star in his own right, Irving won his first and only NBA championship with the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2016 alongside LeBron.

After stints with the Boston Celtics and Brooklyn Nets, Irving returned to the NBA Finals in 2024, as he and Dončić lifted the Mavs before ultimately falling to the Celtics.

The Pistons had the best record in the Eastern Conference last season at 60-22, but they could not make it past the second round of the playoffs, falling in seven games to the Cleveland Cavaliers.

Detroit is returning most of the same key players it had last season, so if there is any drop-off in terms of their regular-season play, perhaps shaking things up by adding a player of Kyrie's caliber could be in the cards.

If so, a "Big 3" of Cunningham, Duren and Irving could help the Pistons rival the stacked starting lineups of the New York Knicks and Philadelphia 76ers in the East.

articles.title: DAZN makes LA Kings part of bigger regional sports vision
articles.summary: NEW YORK— DAZN’s new streaming partnership with the Los Angeles Kings gives fans another way to follow their team without a traditional television subscripti...
articles.body:
NEW YORK— DAZN's new streaming partnership with the Los Angeles Kings gives fans another way to follow their team without a traditional television subscription. For the London-based sports platform, it also provides a foothold in a market where the company hopes to build a much larger presence.

As the NBA and NHL move into their 2026-27 seasons, DAZN is expanding beyond its established business in combat sports, soccer and international distribution. Over the past six months, it has acquired local rights to 19 teams across MLB, the NBA, NHL and WNBA, a collection that includes the Memphis Grizzlies, Minnesota Timberwolves and Indiana Pacers alongside the defending NBA champion New York Knicks, runner-up San Antonio Spurs and Yankees.

DAZN executives told The Sporting Tribune they intend to grow that portfolio. In Southern California, the Kings represent a starting point for a strategy built around bringing more teams, programming and viewing options into one destination.

"Anywhere you can get multiple teams in the same footprint, there's a benefit to that," said Zander Berlinski, DAZN's senior vice president of strategy and business development. "There's a consumer benefit from a singular place to watch the teams you're most likely fans of. There's a business benefit from everywhere from subscriptions to ad sales to economies of scale."

For Kings fans, that strategy begins with a partnership announced last month between DAZN and Angels Broadcast Television. DAZN is the exclusive direct-to-consumer streaming home for available local Kings games beginning this season, while ABTV continues to carry the team through participating cable and satellite providers.

The streaming package includes locally broadcast regular-season games and first-round Stanley Cup playoff games within the Kings' home television territory, which includes Southern California and Hawaii. Nationally exclusive games are excluded.

"We are excited to be partnered with ABTV and DAZN to give Kings fans multiple ways to watch and enjoy Kings hockey this season," Kings president Luc Robitaille said in the partnership announcement. "Whether you're tuning in on cable or streaming with DAZN, our fans will have more access than ever to follow this team all year long."

The standard Kings package costs $129.99 for the season or $19.99 monthly and includes two simultaneous streams in one location, plus downloads. The Ultimate package costs $149.99 for the season or $24.99 monthly and includes five streams across two locations, multiview, downloads, alternate angles and feeds, a one-time 10% discount at the Team LA Store and two complimentary tickets to select games.

Where supported, fans whose television packages include ABTV may also be able to sign into the DAZN app with their provider credentials. That gives the service a role for existing cable customers as well as those purchasing a standalone streaming subscription.

Berlinski said broad availability is central to the company's approach, particularly as fans adjust to another change in how they find their local teams.

"We have a team that is dedicated to maximizing distribution and providing fans with the best viewing experience," Berlinski said. "DAZN is available on every screen with an internet connection, and we have more than 100 distribution partners, from smart TVs and streaming devices to game consoles and web browsers, and we're even integrated into smart cable set-top boxes."

The company sees opportunities to expand its Southern California presence, including a potential relationship with the Angels. Asked about the baseball club, Berlinski expressed interest but did not announce an agreement.

"We'd love to work with the Angels," he said. "They're an amazing organization."

Berlinski said DAZN hopes to bring more baseball teams aboard by the start of next season while continuing discussions across other leagues. Adding teams in markets it already serves is part of how the company evaluates those opportunities.

The 19-team local rights portfolio is one portion of DAZN's broader business. Berlinski said the company also provides technology that powers independently operated team streaming services, including the Vegas Golden Knights' app. Across those different business models, DAZN's portfolio encompasses more than 30 teams.

Walker Jacobs, DAZN's U.S. president and chief revenue officer, said the company wants those relationships to offer more than a place to watch games.

"From standalone subscriptions, flexible plans, and availability on multiple screens to dedicated team hubs and ticketing and merchandise offers, we have built the ultimate fan zone experience," Jacobs said. "You can also bet we're going to be adding enhancements throughout the season."

Berlinski said that includes working with teams to make their own programming available, developing additional original shows and expanding editorial coverage. The goal is to give fans reasons to return between games, with content that reflects the teams they follow.

For now, the immediate test in Southern California is the Kings: making their games accessible, explaining the subscription options and delivering coverage throughout the season. But DAZN's ambitions extend beyond one team and one winter.

"As we look to expand, some of our sort of analysis on where we should focus first is how do we expand potential opportunities to make our current markets even bigger," Berlinski said. "So yeah, very much interested and continue to have conversations with a number of people around the space."

articles.title: Game 7 isn't what haunts Tyrese Haliburton the most about in the 2025 NBA Finals
articles.summary: Pacers' Tyrese Haliburton said Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals isn't what haunts him the most about that series. He told The Ringer what is
articles.body:
Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton joined the Zach Lowe Show on Friday and shared that tearing his Achilles tendon in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals isn't the only thing that haunts him the most about that series.

"I think a lot more about Game 4," said Haliburton, who wore a Fever shirt for the 30-minute interview on The Ringer. "We were winning going into the fourth (quarter, 87-80).

"There were a lot of 1-on-1 possessions between me and (Thunder center) Chet (Holmgren). Elite defender (but) you wish you could get those back, make a better decision, make a better play. I was at my peak in terms of closing. It was four points with (3:20 to play). Closing time. Time to win. I could have done a much better job closing that game."

Pacers and Timberwolves face off during preseason matchup in Iowa

Haliburton missed a layup with the Pacers ahead, 95-93, then made a layup to put them back up 97-95. A pair of Haliburton free throws had Indiana back up 99-97 but he followed with a missed 3-pointer. The Pacers were up 103-99 with 3:20 to play but Haliburton missed a 3 with 1:43 remaining after Oklahoma City had taken a 105-103 lead. The Pacers wouldn't get any closer.

"If we go up 3-1 the pressure of Game 5 changes," Haliburton said of losing Game 4 to tie the series. "That's when I re-aggravated the calf injury. That series was about who could win two in a row. Game 4, we lose that game and lose Game 5, first time we lost two in a row since (March).

"That's the game I wish I could get back more than anything."

articles.title: Warriors reach $14.5 billion valuation, claim NBA’s No. 1 spot over Lakers, Knicks
articles.summary: Stephen Curry has done wonders for the Golden State Warriors franchise. He has not only brought the city of San Francisco four NBA championships since 2015,...
articles.body:
Stephen Curry has done wonders for the Golden State Warriors franchise. He has not only brought the city of San Francisco four NBA championships since 2015, but he has also taken the Warriors from the bottom of the league to the top in total franchise valuation.

The Warriors have been atop the NBA's franchise valuation list for the last six years during the Curry Era, and that has not changed in Sportico's latest valuation projections . Together, the 30 NBA franchises are valued at $199 billion, with the Warriors alone in the No. 1 spot at $14.5 billion, up 28% from their 2025 valuation of $11.3 billion.

Joe Lacob and his ownership group originally purchased the Warriors in July 2010 for an estimated valuation of $450 million, which was a then-record price. Between already having Curry and then drafting both Klay Thompson and Draymond Green, as well as signing Andre Iguodala in 2013 and hiring Steve Kerr as the head coach in 2014, Lacob immediately watched his franchise grow into the league's best.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Since purchasing the Warriors, Lacob has seen this organization grow by over 3,100% over the last 16 years, an increase of $14.05 billion from 2010 to 2026.

Right behind the Warriors are the New York Knicks , valued at $12.8 billion, and the Los Angeles Lakers , valued at $12.5 billion.

The Knicks have long been near the top of the valuations list, and their recent championship run during the 2025-26 season pushed them past the Lakers for the No. 2 spot on this year's rankings.

Following their $10 billion sale to Mark Walter in 2025 , the Lakers ranked second with a valuation of $10 billion. This year, the Lakers are third with a valuation of $12.5 billion, the same amount that the group led by Josh Kushner and Bob Iger bought the LA franchise for from Walter this summer.

Here are the top 10 teams in terms of total valuation entering the 2026-27 NBA season, per Sportico:

The Memphis Grizzlies ranked 30th on Sportico's list with a valuation of $4.2 billion.

Overall, the NBA finds itself in a great spot. The average NBA team is valued at a 14.6 multiple, which is up 13.5 percent from 2025 and the highest multiple among all major North American sports leagues: NFL (12.7), NHL (9.4), MLS (9.2), and MLB (7.2).

During the 2025-26 NBA season, the 30 teams generated an estimated $13.7 billion, which is roughly $456 million per club. That is the second-highest average revenue among the major sports leagues, trailing just the NFL at $733 million.

In terms of the Warriors, their average revenue was far higher than any other organization at $895 million net of their revenue-sharing bill. This was 26% higher than the Knicks' reported revenue.

Between the NBA's new 11-year, $76 billion media deal kicking in , multiple franchises growing into title contenders, and the boom in talent across the nation, the league has never been in a better place.

With expansion talks to Las Vegas and Seattle growing, as well as the league office working on a new local media hub for consumers to watch and engage with games, the NBA is expected to see revenue grow even further than it has. This is especially true with sponsorship deals and advertising revenue exponentially increasing.

articles.summary: The controversial ending to Game 2 of the New York Liberty-Atlanta Dream playoff game is still a hot topic of conversation, with Sophie Cunningham weighing in on Breanna Stewart's criticism of the officiating about a reset timeout.
articles.body:
The controversial ending to Game 2 of the New York Liberty-Atlanta Dream playoff game is still a hot topic of conversation, with Sophie Cunningham weighing in on Breanna Stewart's criticism of the officiating about a reset timeout.

On the latest episode of her No Hesitation podcast (starts at 48:50 mark), Cunningham reacted by saying "that's f--ked" after hearing Stewart's comments after the game.

The situation occurred in the final seconds of overtime with the Liberty trailing 101-98 after Angel Reese made two free throws. New York inbounded the ball and Stewart got a decent look from three to potentially tie the game, but the shot didn't fall as time expired.

Stewart told reporters after the game she was told by two refs that the Liberty didn't have a reset timeout remaining even though they did.

Liberty head coach Chris DeMarco said he was also told they did not have a reset timeout available.

In the pool report conducted by ESPN's Alexa Philippou , lead official Fatou Cissoko-Stephens said referee Kevin Fahy confirmed with his officiating partner New York had a timeout to use.

"Stewart was standing behind referee Fahy when he confirmed with his partner between Reese's penalty free throws that New York did indeed have a reset timeout remaining," Cissoko-Stephens explained.

Cissoko-Stephens added available timeouts are not tracked by officials. Instead, the scorer's table and statistical staff and teams are "responsible for managing and tracking their timeout usage throughout the game."

The Liberty filed an official inquiry with the WNBA about the situation, and the league will follow proper protocols to look into it.

Officiating has been a huge discussion point in the WNBA all season. Cunningham said on her podcast earlier this week one of the refs during the Indiana Fever's series with the Las Vegas Aces told her during Game 3 they "don't know the rules" in response to a situation in the second quarter involving Lexie Hull and Brianna Turner.

Atlanta's victory in Game 2 gave it a 2-0 lead in the best-of-five series against New York. The two clubs will play Game 3 at Barclays Center on Friday at 7:30 p.m. ET.

A win by the Dream would send them to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013.
